text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over several years, and many people have no obvious symptoms in the early stages. When early warning signs do appear, they are usually mild at first.
snippet_highlighted_words: they are usually mild at first

list.snippet: Frequent urination: Needing to go to the bathroom more often, especially at night, as your kidneys try to flush out excess sugar.
Increased thirst: Feeling unusually thirsty or dehydrated because frequent urination drains fluid from your tissues.
Constant fatigue: Feeling tired, sluggish, or weak because your cells cannot effectively absorb and use glucose for energy.
Blurred vision: High blood sugar causing fluid to swell the lenses of your eyes.
Slow-healing wounds: Cuts, bruises, or sores taking a long time to heal due to reduced circulation and minor nerve or immune changes.
Tingling or numbness: A pins-and-needles feeling, burning, or numbness in your hands or feet (early peripheral neuropathy).
Increased hunger or weight changes: Constant hunger despite eating, or unexplained weight loss/gain as the body struggles to process glucose properly.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety, dark patches of skin (acanthosis nigricans) around the neck, armpits, or groin, which signal insulin resistance.
Frequent infections: Recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), yeast infections, or stubborn skin infections.
